terms.gloss: a degree of comparison: positive, comparative, superlative
terms.comment: The positive is gradus positīvus, the comparative comparātīvus, the superlative superlātīvus (Traupman 232, 246); the question is Cujus gradūs comparātiōnis est? (244). gradus and comparātiō are classical, but we have not found the phrase in Lewis & Short, nor positīvus in this sense (Gellius uses it of words fixed by convention). Quintilian speaks of comparatives and superlatives as comparātiōnēs et superlātiōnēs (1.5.45).
gradus positīvus, comparātīvus, superlātīvus, the positive, comparative and superlative degrees; “in the comparative” is in comparātiōne or comparātīvē (Traupman).

phrases.latin: Quot gradūs comparātiōnis sunt adjectīvīs? — Trēs gradūs comparātiōnis.
phrases.english: How many degrees of comparison do adjectives have? — Three degrees of comparison.
What degree of comparison is it? — The positive.
